question.text: What is the minimum number of investors required for an open-ended mutual fund scheme to remain operational?

explanation.text: The Logic: SEBI's "20-25" rule for mutual fund schemes requires every open-ended scheme to maintain a minimum of 20 investors at all times, paired with the cap that no single investor can hold more than 25% of the scheme's corpus. The dual rule ensures genuine pooling of money from a broad investor base and prevents schemes from being run as private vehicles for a few large investors. The Trap: "50 investors" and "100 investors" overstate the regulatory minimum. "10 investors" is below the threshold and would fail the broad-pooling test that distinguishes a mutual fund from a private arrangement. Note: The 20-investor minimum for open-ended schemes is not explicitly stated in the cited NISM Series V-B workbook pages (34, 36, 184, 190); page 34 discusses open-ended operation in general terms. The framing above reflects the broader SEBI regulatory requirement for mutual fund schemes.
